digest.component_or_area: ChatGPT agent guidance and Rebar tracker documentation
propositions: ChatGPT sessions operating in connector-limited environments (missing local clone, Gerrit access, shell network, or mounted Rebar tracker) lack guidance on which operations remain safe and when native ticket creation is impossible.

Native ticket creation is impossible when both the tracker-worktree dimension fails (no accessible `tickets` branch checkout) AND the network/remote dimension fails or native `rebar`/`rebar-mcp` binary is unavailable.

The fallback workflow for impossible-to-create tickets must produce a reviewable NDJSON payload conforming to `export.schema.json`'s required fields (`schema_version`, `ticket_id` as agent-generated UUID4, `ticket_type`, `title`, `status`), plus `description` with Acceptance Criteria and optional `parent_id`, without claiming persistence.

The `rebar import` command is the only sanctioned exceptional ingest mechanism; it accepts NDJSON (not raw event files), assigns fresh local ids/HLC timestamps, preserves source provenance via `source_id`, and is idempotent by `source_id`.

In `rebar import --dry-run` mode, records missing `ticket_id`/`ticket_type` are silently skipped with no warning and no counter increment; only already-imported records increment `skipped`, so malformed records are detectable via `would_create + skipped < total record count`.

A lightweight test must verify that AGENTS.md links to the new ChatGPT guidance, the guidance prohibits GitHub Issues as a tracker substitute and direct Contents-API writes to the `tickets` branch, names `rebar import` as the sole sanctioned exceptional path, and its fallback-payload field list matches `export.schema.json`'s required array.
